title: Gate reviews and approvals
status: gate met - AC-1..AC-6 met: approve is offered only when the gate's other required approvals are recorded and no blocking segregation conflict exists for the actor; a reject or a return without a rationale is refused; a delegated decision records and displays the delegator and the delegate; a second decision for the same step is refused with the original retained; conditions are recorded on the decision and propagated to the subject and its history; and the author of the subject cannot decide it.

dataModel.decision: No new table. The gate IS an approval row in PROCESS_APPROVAL, so a decision writes the row the queue already reads; the checklist is the other approvals of the same step instance; segregation reads the owner's SOD_RULE/SOD_CONFLICT pair; and the delegation columns DELEGATED_FROM/DELEGATED_TO/DELEGATED_BY were already on the approval row, so nothing was added to record it.
dataModel.checklist: A gate's checklist is the other PROCESS_APPROVAL rows of the same PROCESS_STEP_INSTANCE_ID, each satisfied only when its status is APPROVED. The decision being taken is excluded, so a gate cannot block itself.
dataModel.delegation: PROCESS_APPROVAL.DELEGATED_FROM names the delegator and DELEGATED_TO the delegate; a decision writes APPROVED_BY as the delegate and DELEGATED_BY as the delegator, so both names survive on the record.
dataModel.propagation: Conditions are written into the approval's APPROVAL_NOTES and merged into the instance's INSTANCE_DATA_JSON under gateConditions, and the decision is appended to PROCESS_HISTORY as GATE_<kind>.

rules.kinds: APPROVE, APPROVE_WITH_CONDITIONS, RETURN and REJECT. An unknown kind is refused with the list.
rules.rationale: A RETURN or a REJECT without a rationale is refused; an APPROVE_WITH_CONDITIONS without the conditions is refused. A plain approval needs neither.
rules.checklist: Every other approval of the step must be recorded as APPROVED before the gate can be approved; each unsatisfied item names what it is and why.
rules.sod: An unresolved SOD_CONFLICT for the actor only blocks when its SOD_RULE has IS_BLOCKING = 'Y': the owner records that distinction and it is honoured, so an advisory rule is visible but does not disable the decision. A resolved conflict (RESOLVED_DATE set or status RESOLVED) no longer blocks.
rules.author: The instance's creator and the approval's requester are both refused as the decider, so the author of a subject cannot approve their own work.
rules.delegation: When the row records a delegator and delegate, only the delegate may act; a row with a delegator but no delegate cannot be decided by anybody, and both are stated.
rules.single: A gate whose status is anything but empty/PENDING is read-only; the original decision stands and no second decision is written.
rules.ordering: The author and requester checks are applied before the delegation check, so a decision by the requester is reported as their own conflict rather than as a delegation mismatch.

implementation.page: src/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop/Views/GatesPageView.cs (route 'gates': the gate queue, the delegation banner, the checklist grid and text, the blocks panel, the decision state, the decision bar and the prior-decisions grid)

integration.database: SQLite with PROCESS_APPROVAL, PROCESS_STEP_INSTANCE, PROCESS_INSTANCE, PROCESS_DEFINITION, PROCESS_HISTORY, SOD_RULE and SOD_CONFLICT. One gate (PA-1) assigned to nadia on a step of an instance authored by sara and requested by omar, a second required approval (PA-2) assigned to omar, and a blocking segregation rule seeded but not yet conflicted.
integration.ac1_pending: with PA-2 pending, approve is not offered, the blocks text names 'TECHNICAL #2 is not satisfied: it is pending', and an approval attempt is refused with gate-checklist-incomplete without writing a status
integration.ac1_cleared: once PA-2 is recorded as APPROVED by omar, the checklist clears and approve becomes available
integration.sg14_3_sod: adding an open conflict for nadia against a blocking rule disables approve, names the rule and both roles, and the decision is refused with gate-sod-conflict; setting the rule to IS_BLOCKING='N' re-enables it, which proves the owner's flag is honoured
integration.ac2_rationale: a reject with a blank rationale is refused with gate-rationale-required (SG-14-4), and an approval with conditions but no conditions text is refused with gate-conditions-required
integration.ac6_author: a decision by sara, the instance's author, is refused with gate-author-cannot-approve
integration.ac3_delegation: after the row records DELEGATED_FROM sara and DELEGATED_TO nadia, the banner reads 'Acting for sara ... nadia', and a decision by huda is refused with gate-delegated-to-another naming nadia
integration.ac5_conditions: nadia's approval with conditions records APPROVAL_STATUS APPROVED, APPROVED_BY nadia and DELEGATED_BY sara, puts the conditions in APPROVAL_NOTES and in the instance's INSTANCE_DATA_JSON, and appends a GATE_APPROVE_WITH_CONDITIONS history row; the prior-decision entry shows nadia acting for sara
integration.ac4_second: a second decision on the same gate is refused with gate-already-decided, the row still reads APPROVED, and the instance has exactly one gate history row

gates.AC-1 Approve is disabled when the checkl: pass - both refusals are shown as blocks and enforced by the command (SG-14-3).
gates.AC-2 Reject and return require a rationa: pass - refused with the reason before anything is written (SG-14-4).
gates.AC-3 A delegated decision shows delegato: pass - the banner and the record both name them (SG-14-7).
gates.AC-4 A second decision for the same step: pass - the decided gate is read-only and the original is retained.

gates.AC-6 The author of the subject cannot ap: pass - the creator and the requester are both refused.

gateIsAnApprovalRow.finding: The owner has no separate gate table: a gate is a PROCESS_APPROVAL row, and it already carries the delegation columns (DELEGATED_FROM, DELEGATED_TO, DELEGATED_BY, DELEGATION_REASON), the requester, the required action and the decision fields.
gateIsAnApprovalRow.handling: The decision writes the approval row and the checklist is the other approvals of the same step, so no second table and no additive column was needed.

sodBlockingIsTheOwnersFlag.finding: The owner stores IS_BLOCKING and a severity (CRITICAL/HIGH) per rule and records conflicts per user in SOD_CONFLICT with a resolution date.
sodBlockingIsTheOwnersFlag.handling: Only a rule with IS_BLOCKING='Y' disables the decision; a non-blocking rule is shown but does not block, and a conflict with a resolution date or status RESOLVED stops blocking. That keeps the owner's distinction rather than treating every conflict alike.

requesterCheckPrecedesDelegation.finding: The first gateway scenario tested the wrong-delegate rule with omar, who is also the requester, so the refusal came back as gate-author-cannot-approve rather than the delegation error.
requesterCheckPrecedesDelegation.handling: The order of the checks is now stated as a rule, and the scenario uses a third user (huda) for the delegation refusal. Both rules are correct; the test had to address the one it meant.

conditionsNeedAResolvedConflict.finding: After re-enabling the blocking rule, the delegate's approval was correctly refused - the scenario had left the conflict open.
conditionsNeedAResolvedConflict.handling: The scenario resolves the conflict with a compensating control before approving, which is also the path the states table expects for a resolved conflict.

conditionsMustReachTheSubject.finding: Recording conditions only on the approval would leave the subject without them, which is what AC-5 forbids.
conditionsMustReachTheSubject.handling: The conditions are merged into PROCESS_INSTANCE.INSTANCE_DATA_JSON under gateConditions (the original payload is preserved) and the decision is appended to PROCESS_HISTORY; a failure to write either is reported as degraded rather than losing the decision.

limits: Delegation of authority (DELEGATION_OF_AUTHORITY thresholds by entity type and value) is not evaluated: the subject's monetary amount is not recorded on the instance, so the threshold ladder cannot be applied. The feature's person-to-person delegation is what is implemented.

The decision and the propagation are separate writes: the approval is committed first, then the history and the instance data; a failure in the latter two is reported as degraded and the approval still records the decision.
Evidence attachments are not shown or uploaded: the checklist carries evidence references (the approving user), and there is no document store in this build.
The gate's checklist is the other approvals of the step; a gate that requires non-approval evidence (a document, a test) has nowhere to record it, because the owner has no gate-evidence table.
Only SOD_CONFLICT rows already recorded are consulted: the desktop does not run SodEvaluationEngine to detect a new conflict at decision time, so a conflict nobody has evaluated would not block.
An approval row with no PROCESS_STEP_INSTANCE_ID has an empty checklist, so it can be approved whenever nothing else blocks; the owner records step instances for the gates this feature's seed models.
No paging: each read loads the seven tables whole and filters in memory.
No per-command permission enforcement beyond the page gate: workflow.approve is not checked, and the step's required role is not enforced here.
